answer: A useful sybil defense is to make each agent’s influence depend on a scarce, slashable bond, not on how many identities it registers. For example, agents can escrow tokens before endorsing a proposal; if an endorsement is proven to violate a public rule, the bond is forfeited. An attacker can still forge many accounts, but must lock real value behind each one and risks losing it, so splitting one stake among juniper, cedar, and other aliases does not multiply voting power.
